TASK: Preserve the AI-proposed score separately from the instructor-confirmed score, everywhere grades are written. Executable assignment, not a context handoff.

WORKTREE (work ONLY here): C:/Users/basqu/Projects/quest-on.grade-provenance
Branch: feat/grade-provenance. The migration adding the columns already exists at `database/028_grade_provenance.sql` (columns: `grades.ai_proposed_score numeric`, `grades.ai_proposed_at timestamptz`, `grades.ai_proposal_source text`).

=== THE BUG ===
`grades` is one row per (session_id, q_idx) with a single `score` column. Every write goes through a row-wide upsert, so the AI-produced score and the human-confirmed score occupy the same column and the delta is unrecoverable. Worse, the bulk commit path labels AI-produced scores as `grade_type: "manual"`, so even the provenance flag lies.

=== ORDER OF WORK (mandatory) ===
This touches existing behavior, so you write tests BEFORE production code:

STEP 1 — baseline characterization test that PASSES on the unchanged code. Pin the CURRENT observable behavior: after a bulk commit, `grades.score` holds the committed value and `grade_type` is `"manual"`. Run it, capture it PASSING, paste that output.

STEP 2 — failing-first test for the NEW behavior in `__tests__/grade-provenance.test.ts`. It must assert:
  (i) after a bulk-grade commit, `ai_proposed_score` equals the AI-produced score and `ai_proposed_at` is set;
  (ii) after a subsequent instructor edit of that score, `ai_proposed_score` is UNCHANGED;
  (iii) a row whose score came from the AI has a `grade_type` that is NOT `"manual"`.
Run it, capture it FAILING for the right reason (assertion failure, not import/syntax error), paste that output.

STEP 3 — smallest production change that turns it green.

=== FILES IN SCOPE ===
- `app/api/exam/[examId]/bulk-grade/commit/route.ts` (around lines 158-196): writes `score`, `stage_grading`, and `grade_type: "manual"`. Populate the new columns and stop mislabelling AI output as manual.
- `app/api/session/[sessionId]/case-grade/commit/route.ts` (around line 53): same helper, same treatment.
- `app/api/session/[sessionId]/grade/route.ts`: THIS IS THE ONE THAT IS EASY TO MISS. It writes to `grades` DIRECTLY (not through the helper) at roughly lines 137, 528, 556, 658 — this is the instructor editing an individual question's score. Verify each of those is a write (not a read) and make sure none of them clobbers `ai_proposed_score` / `ai_proposed_at` / `ai_proposal_source` back to NULL.
- `lib/grades-upsert.ts`: READ IT to understand the payload shape. Do NOT change its signature — solve this at the call sites.

First run `grep -rn 'grade_type' --include=*.ts app lib __tests__` and handle EVERY consumer of the old value. An index `idx_grades_grade_type` exists, so the value is queried.

=== MUST NOT ===
- Do NOT connect to any database. No `psql`, no `supabase` CLI, no `prisma migrate`, no seed/cleanup scripts. Hard project stop-rule. Mock the Supabase client in tests.
- Do NOT load `.env.local` or read any `.env*` file.
- Do NOT change `lib/grades-upsert.ts`'s exported signature.
- Do NOT remove or rename the existing `"manual"` grade_type value — old rows reference it.
- Do NOT edit files outside the scope list.
- Do NOT add an npm dependency.
- Do NOT add `Co-Authored-By`. Do NOT push.

=== VERIFY (paste real output for each) ===
1. `npx vitest run __tests__/grade-provenance.test.ts`
2. `npx tsc --noEmit`
3. `npm run lint`
4. `git status --short`

=== MANUAL-QA (required — data-shaped, so the auxiliary surface counts) ===
Write a small throwaway node script under `/tmp` that imports nothing from the app but simply prints the exact object literal your commit path now passes to the upsert for an AI-produced grade and for an instructor edit. Run it and paste both objects. The binary observable: the AI-produced object contains `ai_proposed_score` with a non-null value and a `grade_type` that is not `"manual"`; the instructor-edit object does NOT contain `ai_proposed_score` as null. Delete the script afterwards and paste the `rm` receipt.

=== ADVERSARIAL CLASSES to probe and report ===
- stale_state: after your change, does a SECOND edit through a different write path still preserve the proposed value? Show the test that covers it.
- misleading_success_output: do not report a check as passing unless you ran it and are pasting its real output. A green suite that never exercised `session/[sessionId]/grade/route.ts` is not coverage — show which test hits that path.
- dirty_worktree: `git status --short` before you start and after you finish; report both.
State the remaining classes (malformed input, prompt injection, cancel/resume, hung commands, flaky tests, repeated interruptions) as not-applicable with a one-line reason each.

=== COMMIT ===
Message exactly: `fix(grading): AI 제안 점수를 교수 확정 점수와 분리해 보존한다`

STOP WHEN: baseline test captured passing, new test captured failing then passing, all four VERIFY commands pasted with real output, manual-QA objects pasted, cleanup receipt pasted, commit created. Report the commit sha and a DoneClaim listing changed_files, tests, manual_qa, cleanup, risks.
